results.reasoning: Headless rule, judged by the CLI against a throwaway blueprint under a throwaway WALKDOWN_HOME in my scratchpad (never the real home, never the scratch copy on 4730; no browser). Ten rules in one feature file, each declaring a different thing, and `walkdown status --json` read for the derived tiers: a rule saying nothing at all derives verify [agent]; verify: [] and a rule with only signoff: [eng, product] also derive [agent], so nothing short of an excuse removes it; verify: [checks] derives [checks, agent], and no rule got checks without asking (a check must be authored; lint warns that nothing claims it). An excuse under unverifiable.agent removes the tier (verify [] with the excuse shown in the EVIDENCE cell by `walkdown status <rule>`), an excuse under unverifiable.checks leaves agent required, and verify: [agent] beside an agent excuse still derives [] - the excuse wins. One edge worth knowing, kept here rather than failed because lint does surface it: unverifiable.agent set to an empty string or to null also removes the tier (verify []) while excuseFor reads it as no excuse, so that rule's EVIDENCE block prints nothing at all; lint warns 'too thin to argue with (got 0 characters)' but does not error, so a null key is an excuse that says nothing and still excuses. The claim as stated holds on every step.
